task.title: MCP: x_md_get_post / x_md_get_profile raise on null lang (outputSchema says string)
task.body:
## What happens

`x_md_get_post` and `x_md_get_profile` fail on any result where a post carries a null `lang`:

```
RuntimeError: Invalid structured content returned by tool x_md_get_post: None is not of type 'string'

Failed validating 'type' in schema['properties']['posts']['items']['properties']['lang']:
    {'type': 'string'}

On instance['posts'][0]['lang']:
    None
```

The tool call raises instead of returning, even though the server sent a correct result: `result.isError` is `false` and `result.content[0].text` holds the right Markdown.

## Why

The `outputSchema` on both tools declares `posts[].lang` as `{"type": "string"}`, but FxTwitter returns `lang: null` for posts with no detected language. The MCP SDK validates `structuredContent` against the declared `outputSchema` before handing the result back, so validation fails and the client raises — the text content is never reached.

## Repro

```bash
curl -sS -X POST https://mdfromx.com/mcp \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"x_md_get_post","arguments":{"url":"https://x.com/trq212/status/2052809885763747935"}}}'
```

`result.structuredContent.posts[0].lang` is `null`, which fails the tool's own declared schema. It is data-dependent: a post with a detected language (`https://x.com/jack/status/20`, `lang: "en"`) validates fine, so the failure rate tracks how often posts come back without a language tag.

`x_md_search_posts`, `x_md_get_followers` and `x_md_get_following` are unaffected — their payloads do not carry `lang: null`.

## Suggested fix

Either one satisfies the schema the server ships:

- declare `lang` as `{"type": ["string", "null"]}`, or
- omit the key when it is null.

## Impact

Two of the five read tools are unusable in strict clients whenever the payload carries a null `lang` — which is common. Observed against Hermes Agent v0.22.5 on the Python MCP SDK (`mcp/client/session.py`, `_call_tool` output-schema validation); the same validation path is used by other clients built on that SDK, so the blast radius is every strict consumer rather than one harness.

The plain HTTP routes are unaffected — `GET /api/v1/posts` and the permalink form return the same data with no schema validation — so only the MCP structured output is affected.
